cohort: Mothers who delivered babies in a rural hospital in Ghana between 2011 and 2015 (n=412)
finding: While intrapartum antibiotic exposure did not significantly affect birthweight or incidence of birth defects, it was associated with lower mean Apgar scores when administered less than 24 hours before delivery.
mod_finding: After adjusting for method of delivery, perinatal antibiotic use (24 h to delivery) was associated with lower mean Apgar scores.
